description: Does the security skill change what a review finds, or only what it reports?
notes: skill-creator reads skill_name/evals[].{id,prompt,expected_output,files,expectations}. The tier/plants/decoys/gates fields are extra and are what skill-evals/run.ts grades on; skill-creator ignores them.

tiers.textbook: Iteration-1 corpus. Plants are canonical OWASP patterns recognisable on sight. Kept because they are still valid cases, but both arms score 100% on them — not run by default.
tiers.data-flow: Iterations 2-3. Every plant needs a data flow traced across a helper or a second file, and every decoy is code that looks vulnerable and is correct. The gates are calibrated on this tier.

evals.prompt: I'm about to ship the auth service for our blog app. Can you do a security review of the code in that directory and write up what you find?
evals.expected_output: Reports the NoSQL operator injection in the login query, jwt.decode() in place of jwt.verify(), and the hardcoded JWT secret fallback — without flagging the correct register handler, rate limiter, bcrypt cost or env-var Mongo URI.
expectations: Reports MongoDB operator injection: req.body.email reaches User.findOne with no String() cast
Reports jwt.decode() used instead of jwt.verify(), so the signature is never checked
Reports the hardcoded fallback JWT secret

evals.prompt: Security pass on the posts API in that directory before I open the PR, please.
evals.expected_output: Reports the missing ownership check on delete, the mass assignment via Post.create(req.body), and the shell command injection in the PDF export — without claiming auth or pagination bounds are missing.
expectations: Reports the missing ownership/admin check on delete (IDOR)
Reports shell command injection in the PDF export

evals.prompt: Review that directory for security problems — it's the React post page plus the Express app config.
evals.expected_output: Reports the unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML, the reflect-any-origin CORS with credentials, and the unvalidated href allowing javascript: URLs — without flagging VITE_API_URL or plain JSX interpolation.
expectations: Reports the unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML on the post body
Reports CORS origin: true combined with credentials: true
Reports the unvalidated href allowing a javascript: URL

evals.prompt: Security review of the account service in that directory before we ship it.
evals.expected_output: Reports the normalizeIdentifier passthrough enabling operator injection on login, the missing returns making requireAuth fail open, and PATCH /me picking ALLOWED_PROFILE_FIELDS — without flagging the boot-time secret assert, the hashed password-reset flow, or findById on a route param.
expectations: Reports that normalizeIdentifier returns non-string values unchanged, so login passes an attacker-supplied object into User.findOne
Reports that requireAuth calls next() unconditionally — neither the missing-token branch nor the catch returns
Reports that PATCH /me picks ALLOWED_PROFILE_FIELDS, which spreads in role and isActive

evals.prompt: Can you do a security pass on the posts service in that directory before I open the PR?
evals.expected_output: Reports the command injection reaching renderTemplate from exportBranded only, the ownership check comparing against req.body.authorId, and the unescaped RegExp built from the search query — without claiming create/remove/pagination/id-validation are broken.
expectations: Reports command injection: exportBranded passes req.query.template into renderTemplate, which interpolates it into an exec() shell string
Reports that the ownership check in update() compares against req.body.authorId instead of req.user.userId
Reports that buildFilter builds a RegExp from the unescaped search query

evals.prompt: Review that directory for security problems — it's the React post page plus the Express app config.
evals.expected_output: Reports PostView rendering the raw post.body while the sanitized value is used only for the excerpt, the endsWith-based CORS origin match, and the denylist safeUrl — without flagging CommentList, the CSP or the cover image.
expectations: Reports that PostView renders dangerouslySetInnerHTML with the raw post.body while safeBody is used only for the excerpt
Reports that the CORS origin check uses origin.endsWith(host), accepting attacker-registered suffix domains with credentials: true
Reports that safeUrl is a scheme denylist rather than an http/https allowlist
